title: Credit gotchas
objectives: Answer out loud: Why do bond prices fall when rates rise?

blocks.title: What's OID?
blocks.teaser: Original issue discount: debt issued below par (e.g., at 98).
blocks.body: Original issue discount: debt issued below par (e.g., at 98). The lender receives 100 at maturity, so the effective yield is higher than the coupon. It's a way to adjust pricing without changing the stated rate.

blocks.title: Why do bond prices fall when interest rates rise?
blocks.teaser: An existing bond pays a fixed coupon.
blocks.body:
An existing bond pays a fixed coupon. If new bonds pay more, the old one is less attractive, so its price falls until its yield matches the market.

**Interview answer:** "The coupon is fixed, so when new bonds pay more, the old one's price has to fall to offer a competitive yield."

blocks.prompt: Market interest rates rise. What happens to an existing fixed-rate bond?

options.text: Its price falls until its yield matches the market
Its price rises because it's safer
Nothing — the price is fixed at par

blocks.explanation: The coupon is fixed, so when new bonds pay more, the old bond's price has to fall to offer a competitive yield.

blocks.title: Why do yields rise when credit ratings fall?
blocks.teaser: Higher default risk requires higher compensation.
blocks.body: Higher default risk requires higher compensation. The spread over Treasuries widens.

blocks.title: What's covenant-lite and why does it matter?
blocks.body: Loans without maintenance covenants. Borrowers gain flexibility, but lenders lose early warning signals — they can't step in until a payment is missed, which often means lower recoveries.

blocks.title: Investment grade vs. high yield?
blocks.teaser: Investment grade is BBB−/Baa3 or above; below that is high yield ("junk").
blocks.body: Investment grade is BBB−/Baa3 or above; below that is high yield ("junk"). LBO debt is almost always high yield.
